CBSE • CLASS 10 • MATHEMATICS

Mathematics — Question bank

Every question filed on this site, grouped by chapter. Original practice questions written to the syllabus — not official CBSE papers.

Ch 1 Ch 2 Ch 3 Ch 4 Ch 5 Ch 6 Ch 7 Ch 8 Ch 9 Ch 10 Ch 11 Ch 12 Ch 13 Ch 14

Ch 1 · Real Numbers

  • 1 State Euclid’s division lemma.
  • 2 Without performing long division, state whether 13/3125 will have a terminating decimal expansion.
  • 3 Prove that √3 is irrational.
  • 3 The HCF of 96 and 404 is 4. Find their LCM.
  • 4 An army contingent of 616 members marches behind an army band of 32 members. Both groups must march in the same number of columns. What is the maximum number of columns?

Practise with answers →

Ch 2 · Polynomials

  • 2 Find the zeroes of x² − 2x − 8 and verify the relationship with the coefficients.
  • 2 If α and β are the zeroes of 6x² − 3x − 7, find 1/α + 1/β.
  • 3 Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes have sum 1/4 and product −1.
  • 3 If one zero of (k² − 1)x² − 3x + 2 is the reciprocal of the other, find k.

Practise with answers →

Ch 3 · Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables

  • 2 Without solving, tell whether 2x − 3y = 7 and 4x − 6y = 14 have a unique solution.
  • 3 Solve by elimination: 3x + 4y = 10 and 2x − 3y = 1.
  • 5 A boat goes 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream in 10 hours. In 13 hours it can go 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream. Find the speed of the stream and of the boat in still water.
  • 4 Five years ago, Nuri was thrice as old as Sonu. Ten years later, Nuri will be twice as old as Sonu. How old are they?

Practise with answers →

Ch 4 · Quadratic Equations

  • 2 Find the nature of the roots of 2x² − 6x + 3 = 0.
  • 3 Find the value of k for which 2x² + kx + 3 = 0 has two equal roots.
  • 3 Solve 6x² − x − 2 = 0 by factorisation.
  • 5 The sum of the areas of two squares is 468 m². If the difference of their perimeters is 24 m, find the sides of the two squares.

Practise with answers →

Ch 5 · Arithmetic Progressions

  • 2 Find the 20th term from the last term of the AP 3, 8, 13, …, 253.
  • 3 Which term of the AP 3, 15, 27, 39, … will be 132 more than its 54th term?
  • 3 If the sum of the first n terms of an AP is 3n² + 5n, find its 10th term.
  • 5 A sum of Rs 700 is to be used to give seven cash prizes, each prize being Rs 20 less than its preceding prize. Find the value of each prize.

Practise with answers →

Ch 6 · Triangles

  • 1 State the Basic Proportionality Theorem.
  • 2 In ΔABC, DE ∥ BC with AD = 1.5 cm, DB = 3 cm, AE = 1 cm. Find EC.
  • 3 The areas of two similar triangles are in the ratio 9:16. If one side of the smaller triangle is 4.5 cm, find the corresponding side of the larger.
  • 3 Prove that in a right triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

Practise with answers →

Ch 7 · Coordinate Geometry

  • 2 Find the distance between (−2, 3) and (4, −5).
  • 2 Find the point that divides the segment joining (−1, 7) and (4, −3) in the ratio 2:3.
  • 3 Find a relation between x and y if the point (x, y) is equidistant from (3, 6) and (−3, 4).
  • 3 Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1, −1), (−4, 2k) and (−k, 5) if the area is 24/2 square units.

Practise with answers →

Ch 8 · Introduction to Trigonometry

  • 1 Evaluate sin 60° cos 30° + cos 60° sin 30°.
  • 2 If sin A = 3/5, find cos A and tan A (A is acute).
  • 3 Prove that (1 + tan²A)/(1 + cot²A) = tan²A.
  • 3 If tan(A + B) = √3 and tan(A − B) = 1/√3, with 0° < A + B ≤ 90° and A > B, find A and B.

Practise with answers →

Ch 9 · Some Applications of Trigonometry

  • 3 The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 30 m from its foot is 60°. Find the height of the tower.
  • 3 From the top of a 75 m high lighthouse, the angles of depression of two ships on the same side are 30° and 45°. Find the distance between the ships.
  • 4 A person on the bank of a river sees the top of a tree on the opposite bank at an angle of elevation of 60°. Walking 20 m away from the bank, the angle becomes 30°. Find the height of the tree and the width of the river.

Practise with answers →

Ch 10 · Circles

  • 1 How many tangents can be drawn from a point inside a circle?
  • 2 From a point 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm, a tangent is drawn. Find its length.
  • 3 Prove that the lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.
  • 4 A quadrilateral ABCD circumscribes a circle. Prove that AB + CD = AD + BC.

Practise with answers →

Ch 11 · Areas Related to Circles

  • 2 Find the length of an arc of a sector with radius 21 cm and central angle 120°.
  • 3 Find the area of a sector of radius 6 cm with a central angle of 60° (take π = 3.14).
  • 3 Find the perimeter of a sector with radius 14 cm and central angle 90°.
  • 4 A square of side 14 cm has a circle inscribed in it. Find the area between the square and the circle.

Practise with answers →

Ch 12 · Surface Areas and Volumes

  • 3 A solid consists of a cylinder with a hemisphere on one end and a cone on the other, all of radius 7 cm. The cylinder is 20 cm high, the cone 12 cm high. Find the total surface area (take π = 22/7).
  • 3 A solid metallic sphere of radius 4.2 cm is melted and recast into a cylinder of radius 6 cm. Find the height of the cylinder.
  • 4 100 solid iron spheres, each of radius 1 cm, are melted to form one solid sphere. Find its radius.
  • 4 A frustum of a cone has radii 14 cm and 7 cm and height 24 cm. Find its slant height and curved surface area (take π = 22/7).

Practise with answers →

Ch 13 · Statistics

  • 2 Find the class mark of the class 25–35.
  • 3 Find the mean of the data: class intervals 0–10, 10–20, 20–30, 30–40 with frequencies 3, 5, 7, 5.
  • 4 Find the median of the distribution: 0–10 (f = 4), 10–20 (f = 6), 20–30 (f = 10), 30–40 (f = 8), 40–50 (f = 2).
  • 3 Find the mode of the data: 10–20 (f = 3), 20–30 (f = 12), 30–40 (f = 9).
  • 4 The mean of the distribution 0–10 (f = 5), 10–20 (f = f), 20–30 (f = 8), 30–40 (f = 7) is 20.5. Find f.

Practise with answers →

Ch 14 · Probability

  • 1 A card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck. What is the probability that it is a red king?
  • 2 A die is thrown once. Find the probability of getting (i) a prime number, (ii) a number greater than 4.
  • 3 Two dice are thrown together. Find the probability that the sum is 9.
  • 2 A bag contains 5 red and 3 green balls. One ball is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is not red.
  • 3 A card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled deck. Find the probability that it is (i) a face card, (ii) neither a king nor a red card.

Practise with answers →
